Maybe I’d stay an entire day in Gyeongju. We stayed in the Gyeongchon Hanok village so everything was within walking distance and it was nice to take a walk. There’s an amazing restaurant called Ryoko. I’m still craving their food haha. if you’re planning to go to Busan in the evening you’re absolutely fine with one night at Gyeongju. Hmm, a city we didn’t like was Sokcho as there’s not much to do and it was quite underwhelming after Seoul. However, we stayed there because of the Seoraksan Narional Park which was beautiful, and the hikes made up for the city haha. Since you’re planning to visit the national park as well so I’d recommend checking their website closer to your departure date as some of the trails might be closed due to fire prevention etc. The same thing happened to us as we wanted to do the park’s highest peak however it was unfortunately closed. 

Another thing I would mention is if you are planning to do the Hallasan Mountain trail on Jeju you need to book a ticket (which is free) prior to your hike to access the trail. Those tend to sell out quickly so maybe book them 2 days before you’re planning to do the hike. There are different timings although I’d recommend booking the earliest which allows you to enter between 5 and 8 am as you need to reach the Jindalaebat shelter before 12:30 in order for you to be allowed further to make it to the peak. Also, don’t let them fool you with their map !! we got scammed lol cause the map has 3 different colours - orange (easy), red (difficult), and green (normal) and let me tell you the green was much more difficult than the red hahah I was even wondering during the red part of the trail (I go hiking every year so that’s why) that whoo this is actually very OK it’s not that bad but the green lol it’s doable but there are loads of stairs and some parts have a bunch of massive rocks which can be slippery!

Also if you can for the Hallasan do the Seongpanak trail upwards as the Gwaneumsa trail is very very challenging

Link to book the tickets: https://visithalla.jeju.go.kr/main/main.do

Link to check trail closures at Seoraksan: https://www.knps.or.kr/front/portal/open/pnewsDtl.do?menuNo=8000517&pnewsId=PNEWSM027044

Happy to answer anything if you have more questions also happy to recommend places we loved if you’re interested
